subject: physics
question_text: Can a simple pendulum be used in an artificial satellite?

verification.note: The mark split is invented and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The question itself is sourced, not invented. AI physics check 2026-08-24: formulas, signs, numbers and claims verified against NCERT Class-11 conventions; corrections applied to explanation text (why / common_mistakes / memory_tip), marked answer lines unchanged unless factually wrong.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The answer
lines: A simple pendulum will not oscillate at all
inside an artificial satellite, so it cannot
be used to measure time there.
steps.why: The bob needs something to pull it back to the mean position; inside a satellite nothing does.
common_mistakes: Answering yes and saying it would simply swing more slowly.

recall.must_convey: That the answer is no, a simple pendulum will not oscillate inside a satellite.

steps.memory_tip: The answer is no — say it first, then give the reason.

steps.label: The reason
lines: Inside an orbiting satellite everything is in
free fall together, so the effective value of
g acting on the bob is zero.
An infinite period means no oscillation.
steps.why: The satellite and the bob fall around the earth at the same rate, so relative to the satellite the bob feels no pull at all.
common_mistakes: Saying there is no gravity in orbit — there is; the satellite and the bob are simply falling together.
Putting the value of g at the satellite's height into T = 2π√(l/g). The bob responds to the effective g inside the satellite, which is zero; the local field value does not set the period.

recall.must_convey: That the effective g is zero in free fall, so T is 2 pi root l by zero, which is infinite.

steps.memory_tip: Inside the satellite everything is in free fall: effective g is zero, so T = 2π√(l/g) has no meaning — the bob never swings back.
